note: File to Media has NO settings form, no config schema, no permissions of its own, no Drush, no plugin types. It exposes (1) a Views field on the file_managed table with id/field/plugin_id 'file_to_media' (registered by hook_views_data_alter) that renders a 'Create <media type>' dropbutton, and (2) route file_to_media.add_form at /file/to-media/{file}/{media_type} (permission 'access files overview'). Medium/hard cases are grounded ONLY in Views config (safe: no media types / field storages are created) — building or inspecting a view based on file_managed that carries the file_to_media field. All views are namespaced ftm_*.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the file_to_media module enabled, how do I give content editors a way to turn existing managed files into Media entities? What does the module actually add?
evals.expected_output: Add the module's Views field 'File to Media links' (plugin file_to_media, on the file_managed base table) to a view of files. Each file row then shows a 'Create <media type>' dropbutton that opens the media add-form at /file/to-media/{file}/{media_type}.

evals.prompt: With file_to_media, why might the 'Create media' link not appear for a particular file in the view? What conditions must a file and a media type meet?
evals.expected_output: The dropbutton is hidden if the file is private (not downloadable by anonymous) or already used by a media entity. A 'Create <type>' link only appears for media types the user can create whose source (file) field's file_extensions include the file's extension.

evals.prompt: What is the route and permission behind file_to_media's conversion form, and what does the controller do when you open it for a file and a media type?
evals.expected_output: Route file_to_media.add_form at /file/to-media/{file}/{media_type}, permission 'access files overview'. The controller checks create access + that the file is public + that the media type's source field accepts the extension, then builds a media entity with the file on the source field and returns its add-form.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a View configured with file_to_media's 'Create media' button field. Inspect the live view configuration and give the machine name of that view.
evals.expected_output: The view is ftm_known_view: its display has a field handler with plugin_id 'file_to_media' on the file_managed base table.

evals.prompt: A view named ftm_second_view on this site uses file_to_media. Inspect its configuration and report the plugin id of the field handler that renders the create-media dropbutton and the path of its page display.
evals.expected_output: The field handler's plugin_id (and table/field) is file_to_media on file_managed, and the page display is served at /ftm-second.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a View with machine name ftm_files based on the Files data (base table file_managed) and add the file_to_media 'File to Media links' field (the Views field whose plugin is file_to_media) so each file row shows a Create-media dropbutton. Save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A views.view.ftm_files config entity exists whose base_table is file_managed and which has a field handler with plugin_id 'file_to_media'.

evals.prompt: This site already has a View named ftm_target_view listing files (base table file_managed) but it does NOT yet offer file-to-media conversion. Add the file_to_media 'File to Media links' field (plugin file_to_media) to that view and save it, so editors can convert each file to a media entity.
evals.expected_output: views.view.ftm_target_view now has a field handler with plugin_id 'file_to_media' (table file_managed) in one of its displays, in addition to whatever fields it already had.
